transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-05-19 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lisa Thompson (Harbor Sec Lead), Raj Patel (CTO), Emily Nguyen (Compliance)

Summary: quick SOC2/ISO posture review, details on trust center, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO, logs, KMS.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, account lead, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Lisa: Good, thanks. Ready to go.
[00:08] Raj: All good, thanks.
[00:10] Maya: Great. So the goal today is to walk through our SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture, give you access to the trust center, and answer any controls mapping questions you have. Emily I know you had some pre-submitted items?
[00:22] Emily: Yeah, mostly around evidence access — like do we get the full report, how do we pull audit logs, and specifically encryption key management, KMS, H S M questions. Also curious about regional data residency.
[00:34] Diego: Cool, we'll cover those. I'll start with the reports. Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II that covers our hosted and dedicated services in scope, and we also have ISO 27001 with the certificate and statement of applicability. We usually provide the org-level PDFs plus access to the trust center for more granular evidence.
[00:52] Lisa: When you say "trust center access" — is that an account in your console? How granular is it, can we download artifacts for specific controls?
[00:59] Diego: Yes, it's a read-only UI. We can grant a Harbor security group access; you can filter by control, timeframe, and download the artifact packages. It includes control owners, evidence attachments, and auditor notes from the last assessment.
[01:15] Lisa: Ok, and retention on those artifacts, like how long do you keep evidence?
[01:19] Diego: We keep raw evidence and auditor packages for 3 years by default in the trust center, with the summary reports kept indefinitely. If you need extended retention we can discuss archival options.
[01:28] Raj: For our audit we need the raw logs for 2 years at minimum — syslogs, admin actions — can you export to S3 or push to our SIEM?
[01:36] Diego: Yes. Audit logs (console admin APIs, auth events, provision, role changes) can be exported via our log export to your S3 bucket, or we can set up a streaming forwarder to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog). Exports support gzip and json-lines.
[01:51] Emily: Is there a retention policy on the platform level separate from trust center evidence? Like production audit logs retention?
[01:58] Diego: Default retention for operational audit logs is 90 days in the UI, but you can configure long term exports. For trust center evidence it's separate.
[02:05] Lisa: Ok makes sense. Another area — RBAC and SSO. We use Okta and want SAML/SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained roles so our auditors can see separation of duties.
[02:18] Maya: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC, and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based with admin, auditor, developer, read-only, and we also have resource-level roles for model endpoints and trust center access.
[02:31] Lisa: Can you map those roles to Harbor's internal roles? We need an audit trail of who did what, and least privilege.
[02:39] Diego: Yes — we provide role mapping during onboarding. And every role change and impersonation or token issuance is logged. The logs include user id, action, resource, timestamp, and request id.
[02:50] Speaker 2: mm-hmm, and we also have API key rotation, um, we recommend using short-lived tokens for automation.
[02:58] Raj: Quick question on API keys vs OAuth tokens — are keys visible in the console after creation?
[03:04] Diego: No, API keys are only shown at creation time. After that they're hashed and can't be retrieved — rotate if lost. We support key rotation via API.
[03:12] Emily: Good. On encryption — do you manage keys or do we bring our own key (BYOK)?
[03:17] Diego: We support both. By default we use platform-managed KMS keys in the region, but customers can use BYOK backed by HSMs, or connect to their cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). We also support an HSM gateway for dedicated/private deployments.
[03:33] Lisa: How is key rotation handled for BYOK? If we rotate in our KMS does Redwood pick it up automatically?
[03:39] Diego: For cloud KMS we use a reference to the KMS key ARN; when you rotate keys within your KMS that's fine as long as the key alias remains. For BYOK with exported key material managed by HSM, we have a process to update key material — we'll coordinate with your ops.
[03:53] Raj: Are encryption metrics and key usage available in logs? We need to show in our compliance evidence who decrypted and where.
[03:59] Diego: Yes, key usage events are in the audit logs and the trust center evidence includes crypto operation summaries (decrypt requests, signer, timestamps). We can also provide KMS audit trails depending on integration.
[04:10] Lisa: For ISO scope — does it cover both hosted and dedicated? We might want to go dedicated for some PHI workloads.
[04:17] Maya: Our ISO certificate covers the control plane and hosted products in scope listed on the certificate. Dedicated/reserved capacity has control overlap, and we provide scoping details in the SoA (statement of applicability). I'll share the SoA and we can map which systems are in-scope for Harbor.
[04:31] Emily: Great. Can you walk through a sample control mapping? For example, Access Control and SOD controls — how do you provide evidence?
[04:40] Diego: Sure. For access control we attach IAM config snapshots, admin change logs, and internal policy docs. For SOD we include role matrix, provisioning tickets, and auditor test results. Evidence items have timestamps and are cross-referenced to control IDs.
[04:53] Lisa: Sometimes your control IDs don't exactly match our SOC mapping — do you provide a crosswalk file?
[04:59] Diego: Yes we provide a controls crosswalk mapping Redwood controls to SOC2 and ISO controls. We can produce a Harbor-specific mapping as well.
[05:08] Raj: On the legal side — you mentioned audit talks and redaction — if we share customer data in an audit package how is it redacted?
[05:15] Maya: We redact any customer PII from auditor packages; trust center artifacts contain metadata and references, not raw PII. If auditors need raw artifacts, we have an established process with NDA and scoped access.
[05:26] Emily: For our internal audit we need exportable evidence in CSV or PDF. Is that supported?
[05:31] Diego: Yes. Downloads support PDF for reports and zip packages for evidence; CSV/JSON for logs.
[05:36] Lisa: About pen tests and vuln scans — are results included in trust center?
[05:40] Diego: Pen test summaries and remediation attestations are included; full reports are shared under NDA. We maintain quarterly vuln scanning and weekly critical patching evidence.
[05:48] Speaker 1: hmm.
[05:50] Maya: Anything else on reports?
[05:52] Emily: One operational question: do you have a change management timeline? For example, if Redwood changes encryption defaults or introduces new infra, how are customers notified?
[06:02] Diego: Yes, we publish a change log and a deprecation schedule in the console, and for major security-related changes we send a customer security bulletin and a 90-day deprecation timeline. Also we have a security advisories subscription.
[06:15] Raj: Network segmentation — for private deployments can we require air-gapped or VPC peering only?
[06:22] Diego: For Private deployments yes, we support VPC-only connectivity and on-prem air-gapped installs. For Dedicated we have customer-dedicated subnets and strict egress controls.
[06:33] Lisa: Data residency — can you guarantee that production data for Harbor will stay in us-east-1 and eu-west-1?
[06:40] Maya: Yes, you can pin region routing policies. We'll ensure primary region residency; failover policies can be restricted to specified regions per contract. We'll document the region SLAs.
[06:54] Emily: What about backups — are they encrypted and stored in the same region?
[06:59] Diego: Backups are encrypted and can be configured to stay in the same region; cross-region backups are optional and will be called out in the contract.
[07:08] Lisa: On legal/compliance logs — retention for auth logs vs app logs, can we set different policies?
[07:14] Diego: Yes, retention is configurable per log type. We can set long-term exports to your bucket for auth logs, and shorter retention for debug traces.
[07:24] Raj: Let's dig into a few real examples — Emily, do you want to surface the top 3 control questions?
[07:29] Emily: Sure — one, evidence access and export; two, KMS/BYOK and key ownership; three, RBAC/SSO mapping and audit trails.
[07:38] Maya: Perfect — we'll cover each. For evidence access, I'll send the SOC2 Type II PDF and ISO cert plus trust center invite. For KMS, Diego will follow up with integration notes. For RBAC/SSO, Diego will send the SCIM mapping template.
[07:51] Diego: I'll also put together a short doc on key rotation and HSM gateway flows for dedicated/private. It will include diagrams and sample IAM policies.
[07:59] Lisa: One more question on audit scope: do your SOC 2 auditor tests include configuration drift checks?
[08:06] Diego: Some, yes. We have automated configuration monitoring and detect drift; auditor samples include drift remediation evidence.
[08:13] Speaker 2: also, our internal compliance team logs change tickets in Jira which are included in evidence attachments.
[08:20] Raj: If we go dedicated for PHI, what changes in scope and responsibility?
[08:26] Diego: For dedicated there's increased customer control over networking and keys; Redwood still manages the runtime and core control plane unless you choose private where you own the infrastructure. We'll provide an explicit responsibilities matrix (RACI) showing which controls shift to Harbor.
[08:40] Emily: Good — please include that RACI in the mapping.
[08:43] Maya: Will do.
[08:44] Lisa: Can you confirm your subprocessor list and whether any third parties have access to raw logs?
[08:50] Maya: We'll share the subprocessors list. By default subprocessors don't get raw logs; access is limited and audited. Any vendor access is recorded in the trust center.
[08:59] Emily: Great. A small nit — naming conventions on audit entries sometimes differ from our schema. Can you include a mapping or sample payload?
[09:07] Diego: Yes, I'll include a sample log payload and field mapping.
[09:11] Raj: About SLAs — for security incidents what's your response time commitments?
[09:17] Maya: For critical incidents we have a 1-hour acknowledgement SLA and a 24-hour initial report. We can include more aggressive incident response in the enterprise contract.
[09:28] Lisa: Do you provide forensic packages post-incident?
[09:32] Diego: Yes, for customers with the incident response add-on we provide forensic artifacts and support.
[09:37] Speaker 1: okay.
[09:39] Emily: Ok those are the main items. Can we have the trust center access before the end of this week?
[09:45] Maya: Yes we can get that done. Diego will provision.
[09:48] Diego: I'll create the Harbor security group and send invites after this call, targeting today.
[09:54] Maya: Awesome. Any concerns about data residency binding or contractual language?
[09:59] Raj: We'll review the contract but expect to require region-binding clause for production PHI workloads.
[10:06] Maya: Noted — we'll engage legal on the region-binding language.
[10:10] Lisa: One last thing: can you include a timeline for the controls mapping work? We need to present to internal audit in two weeks.
[10:18] Emily: Yeah two weeks works if we get the SOC2/ISO artifacts and the mapping template ASAP.
[10:24] Maya: We'll prioritize. I'll send artifacts by Thursday (2026-05-21) and Diego will get trust center done by Friday (2026-05-22).
[10:31] Diego: Also tagging the PRD to include dedicated controls mapping -- I'll attach sample SoA and crosswalk.
[10:37] Raj: Sounds good.
[10:39] Maya: Great — thanks everyone. Recap: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO, Diego to invite to trust center and share KMS notes and SCIM mapping, Harbor to share controls template and confirm residency. We'll schedule a follow-up deep-dive on KMS/HSM next week.
[10:55] Lisa: Thanks, talk soon.
[10:57] Raj: Thanks all.
[10:59] Maya: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
